chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), said:

I asked him about the expiation for an oath, in the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'but whosoever cannot find (means) then fasting for three days.' What is the limit of the one who does not find? And if a man is asked about what is in his hand, and he finds it? He said: 'When there is no excess with him beyond the livelihood of his family, then he is from those who do not find.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of 'not finding' means for expiating an oath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refines the legal definition of 'insolvency' (la yajid) by anchoring it to the threshold of family subsistence rather than absolute poverty, ensuring that those with surplus wealth cannot evade the financial penalty. This interpretation aligns with the Shia juristic principle that kaffarah obligations are proportional to one's capacity, preventing hardship for the genuinely needy while maintaining accountability for the affluent. The ruling underscores the Quranic emphasis on justice and the prioritization of family welfare in Islamic financial jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan Bin yahya, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahimasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about an expiation for the oath in the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [5:89] but whosoever cannot find (means) then fasting for three days. What is the limit of the one who does not find, and if the man were to be asked with regarding to what is in his hand, and he finds it’. So heasws said: ‘When there does not happen to be with him any excess from the livelihood of his family, so he is from the ones ‘who cannot find’’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the expiation for oath mentioned in the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘. . . if one cannot find then it is three days fasting.’ [5:91] and about the limit of ‘if one cannot find’ and that a man asks for help (beggar) but he is not of ‘if one cannot find’.
He (the Imam) said, ‘If one does not have more than what his dependents need, then “if one does not find” applies to him.’”
